result.headline: Throttle commanded to 0 at 101.25 s; motor channel 2 followed and the aircraft lost altitude.
result.explanation: A control fault shows on the throttle/motor channel 2 loop at about 101.25 s. The throttle command dropped to 0 first and ch2 followed to 1100 us. Who commanded it is not in the recording.

evidence.quote: CHANGE propulsion.throttle at t=101.254 s: 59.5 -> 0 % (step -59.5, 59.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The throttle command was cut from about 60% to 0 in one step, with no mode change or event recorded.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[2]] at t=101.297 s: 1576 -> 1100 us (step -476, 59.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Motor channel 2 dropped to its minimum 43 ms after the throttle step, so it followed the command.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=101.254 s to the end of the recording (7.779 s, 21 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle never recovered. Earlier manoeuvres came back, so this is not a manoeuvre.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.985 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch2 is the propulsion output, so the loop that failed is throttle/ch2.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=100.164 s: median 50.137 before, 41.442 after m
evidence.shows: After the cut, altitude fell from about 50 m to 13 m by 109 s, with pitch and roll swings. These are effects of lost thrust.

checked.check: Which signals left baseline first around the cut (t=95-109 s)
checked.result: Throttle left baseline at 101.254 s and ch2 at 101.725 s. Altitude left at 104.527 s, after both.
checked.about: Throttle command is the earliest sign; altitude loss is an effect

checked.result: Throttle went 46 -> 0 %, ch2 1468 -> 1100 us with zero spread. Other motor channels stayed at about 1506-1513 us.
checked.about: The fault is isolated to the throttle/ch2 loop

checked.check: Window 96-109 s on throttle, ch2, altitude and attitude
checked.result: Throttle ramped 45 -> 64 % until 100.5 s, then 0 from 101.254 s. Altitude held about 48-50 m until 103 s, then fell to 13 m.

checked.check: Compare at the early velocity shift (12.944 s)
checked.result: No freeze and no tracking change (pitch tracking ratio 0.98, roll 1.11). The velocity shifts are manoeuvres.
checked.about: Early velocity shifts and attitude-tracking anomalies are not the fault

checked.result: Only start-up events at 0.684 s (low voltage warning, sensor health error). No earlier cases are available.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=100.164 s: median 50.137 before, 41.442 after m
effects.why: Altitude loss follows the throttle cut.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.attitude[pitch] changed level for good at t=100.161 s: median -0.525 before, -16.25 after deg
effects.why: The pitch-down setpoint and attitude follow the loss of thrust.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.altitude[relative] at t=105.474 s: 45.509 -> 27.129 m (step -18.38, 83.9x its usual variation)
effects.why: This is the rapid descent after the cut.

next_action.why: The recording does not show who set throttle to 0. This separates a commanded or failsafe cut from a power or motor fault.

outcomes.label: Mode change or failsafe at 101.25 s
outcomes.means: The throttle cut was commanded by autopilot logic, so look at its trigger (RC link, geofence, battery failsafe).

outcomes.label: Voltage sag or brownout before 101.25 s
outcomes.means: Power system limited thrust and the controller cut throttle in protection.

outcomes.label: No event, voltage normal, ESC fault flag
outcomes.means: Propulsion hardware on ch2 or the ESC is the likely place.

unknowns: Who or what set throttle to 0 at 101.254 s; no mode or failsafe event is recorded there.
Battery voltage is not in the recording, so power cannot be ruled in or out.
Airspeed (0) and yaw rate (0) are constant throughout, so those sensors give no information.

already_answered.question: When did the control fault occur?
already_answered.answer: At 101.254 s the throttle command dropped to 0 and stayed there. ch2 followed at 101.297 s.
already_answered.quote: CHANGE propulsion.throttle at t=101.254 s: 59.5 -> 0 % (step -59.5, 59.5x its usual variation)

already_answered.question: Where on the aircraft was the fault?
already_answered.answer: The throttle/propulsion loop on actuator channel 2. Channels 1, 3, 4 and 5 kept moving.
already_answered.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.985 over the recording): it serves that loop

already_answered.question: Did a mode change or failsafe event trigger it?
already_answered.answer: No. The only two events are start-up warnings at 0.684 s.

data_requests.what: Autopilot log: mode, failsafe, RC and battery voltage and current
data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded cut, a power fault and a motor or ESC fault.

unobservable.fact: Condition of the ch2 motor, ESC and wiring
unobservable.why_it_matters: A motor or ESC fault would explain the loss of propulsion if the throttle cut was protective.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the ESC and motor and read the ESC fault log.

hypotheses.claim: Autopilot, failsafe or operator set throttle to 0 at 101.25 s, and ch2 followed.
hypotheses.because: Throttle stepped to 0 before ch2 changed, with no recorded event. The commanded value is the earliest sign.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller throttle command and actuator output

hypotheses.claim: The ch2 motor or ESC failed or protected itself, causing the throttle drop.
hypotheses.because: ch2 followed the throttle command, so the cut is upstream of the output. The motor itself is not observed.

hypotheses.claim: A power limit led to a protective throttle cut.
hypotheses.because: A low voltage warning exists at start-up (0.684 s) but battery voltage is not recorded. Cannot be ruled in or out.

hypotheses.claim: The roll, pitch or yaw loops caused the fault.
hypotheses.because: Large roll setpoints recur at 23, 69 and 101 s and tracking holds. The swings after 101 s follow the throttle cut.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor fault, such as the start-up sensor health error, drove the cut.
hypotheses.because: The sensor health error appears only at start-up (0.684 s). Nothing changed in the sensor-derived signals before the cut except manoeuvres.
hypotheses.observed_at: events and compare at candidate times

events.what: Throttle command cut to 0 and held
events.why: Earliest sign of the fault, with no recorded mode or failsafe event.
